newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch see new mobile phone licence auction in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Dutch see new mobile phone licence auction in 1997.

text.p: The Dutch telecoms and transport ministry said on Thursday it planned during 1997 to auction a licence for a DCS 1800 digital mobile phone network.

A ministry spokesman said the move depended on discussions in parliament but said the ministry planned to issue a licence by July 1 next year, the date the government envisages open competition in Dutch telephony. The EU aims to liberalise telephony in most member states by the beginning of 1998.
The spokesman said no particular auction method had yet been finalised. "I think we expect the further discussions in parliament in January or February to resolve that," he said.
He said competition for the new licence would be open internationally with former state telecoms monopolist Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV (KPN) and GSM licence-holder Libertel excluded.
"They already have licences for GSM (Global System for Mobile communications) and the minister prefers more open competition so they're excluded for this licence," he said.
Libertel, which late last year became the first competitor to KPN with its new digital GSM service, combines financial company ING and British mobile phone company Vodafone Group Plc.
DCS 1800 offers a similar digital mode of mobile telephony to the GSM standard but operates on a higher frequency and with network radio cells built closer together.
Analysts say this makes a network more expensive to build but offers greater capacity, making it an ideal technology for cities and conurbations.

Telecoms providers in the Netherlands have expressed interest in interlacing DCS 1800 technology into fixed line telephony, offering "seamless" switching between a subscriber's mobile and hard-wired phones. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
